resources.string: FocusLock shows a focus screen over apps that are restricted: apps your teacher locked during class focus time, or apps you chose for your own focus session. It only checks which app is currently in front. It does not read, record or send what is on your screen.
ON: FocusLock can restrict your selected apps.
Enabled, but the service is still starting. Wait a moment.
OFF: FocusLock cannot restrict apps yet.

FocusLock needs Android\'s Accessibility service to notice which app is in front, so it can show the focus screen over the apps you chose. It does not read your screen content and sends nothing anywhere.

FocusLock uses Android's Accessibility service only to detect which app is currently in front, so it can cover the apps you selected with a focus screen. It does not read text or content on your screen, and nothing is sent anywhere.

In the next screen, open the list of installed or downloaded apps, choose FocusLock, and switch it on. On Android 13 or newer, an app installed outside Google Play may first need Allow restricted settings (Settings, Apps, FocusLock, three-dot menu).

Then come back here and start your session.
